subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Serpent
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Serpent usable.

hook.text: The snake tempted Eve, guarded treasure in Greece, and created the world in Aboriginal Australian lore.

buildup.text: Snakes shed skin and appear reborn. That visual trick made them symbols of immortality and renewal.

discovery.text: In Hindu myth, Shesha the serpent holds the universe on its coils. The snake supports all existence.

twist.text: Christianity cast the serpent as pure evil. But in medicine, the snake on the staff still means healing.

climax.text: Feared and worshipped, the serpent is the most contradictory symbol in mythology. Hero and villain.

punchline.text: Shed your skin. Be reborn. Or be damned.

quiz.question: Why did many cultures associate snakes with immortality?
options: They shed their skin and appear reborn
